question: Does a task written as a design conversation (few reads asked for, one-line answers) hold enough context and enough thinking for thinking-cutting to be tested on it: does its context pass the 140k trigger, and how much thinking does it hold by then?
rule: One task, bug-hunt-long: eleven reports of real MLflow bugs (twelve upstream fixes) given one at a time as symptoms over twenty-seven turns, short answers asked for, on the commit before the oldest fix. It is bug-hunt-six (sized 2026-11-17: 143 calls, 141k peak on the last turn, 26k of thinking, too short for a cut to matter) with five more reports and recall turns after them. Written 2026-11-17 before any run. One session with no proxy, to size it; not a comparison.
